name: AARP Foundation Tax-Aide (free tax prep – Durham, Raleigh & Apex sites)
description: Free tax preparation and e-filing of federal and NC returns by IRS-certified volunteers. Runs each year from about February to mid-April.
hours: Tax season only (about Feb–Apr). The 2027 schedule isn't posted yet.
access: Free. You don't have to be an AARP member. Focus is on people over 50 and people with low to moderate income. Appointments required. Bring Social Security cards for everyone on the return.
notes: Locations in the 2026 season: (1) Durham Main Library, 300 N. Roxboro St., Durham 27701, Jan 30–Apr 13, 2026. Book online through the library's tax page, call 919-695-7548 or email durhamtaxaide@gmail.com, and don't call the library (https://durhamcountylibrary.org/arbitrary-feature/tax-preparation/). (2) Raleigh Tax-Aide, which is moving to Trinity Baptist Church, 4815 Six Forks Rd, Raleigh 27609. Appointments are online only at raleightaxaide.com and open in January 2027. Email trinitybaptist.taxaide@gmail.com. (3) Apex Senior Center, 63 Hunter St., Apex 27502, Feb 3–Apr 14, 2026, Tue 9:30–2:30 and Thu 9:30–5:30. Book in person during site hours, not online. Call 919-446-1348 (https://apexnc.org/DocumentCenter/View/53220). AARP's national site said service was closed for the 2026 season when checked. Use its site locator for other Wake sites once 2027 sites are posted. Out-of-scope returns can't be prepared.

name: Orange County VITA – free tax prep (Department on Aging, Volunteer Connect 55+)
description: Free federal and NC income tax preparation by IRS-certified volunteers, run by Orange County's Department on Aging.
hours: Appointment line is open Jan 12–Apr 15. Booking for the 2027 season opens around Jan 15, 2027.
access: Free for people with low to moderate income, of any age and from any county. By appointment, by phone or online.
notes: The county page said the 2026 season had ended and that phone and online booking reopen around Jan 15, 2027. The 2027 site schedule isn't posted yet. For the 2025 season, in-person sites were the Seymour Center (2551 Homestead Rd, Chapel Hill, on a bus route) and the Passmore Center (Hillsborough), per UNC Student Legal Services (https://www.uncstudentlegal.unc.edu/copy-of-organizations-we-work-with). The 919-245-4242 appointment line is staffed by volunteers. To volunteer, call 919-245-4240.

name: Chatham County Aging Services – VITA free tax prep
description: Free basic income tax preparation by IRS-certified volunteers through the IRS VITA program, run by Chatham County Aging Services.
address: Pittsboro Center for Active Living, 365 Highway 87 North, Pittsboro, NC 27312
hours: Tax season only (about Feb–Apr), by appointment. The 2027 schedule isn't posted yet.
access: Free for people with low to moderate income, of any age. By appointment.
notes: A Feb 4, 2026 Sanford Herald article confirmed Aging Services was booking 2026 VITA appointments. In past seasons it held them in Pittsboro (the address above), at the Siler City Center for Active Living (112 Village Lake Rd, Siler City) and at Goldston Town Hall. In 2024 the VITA booking line was 919-542-4512 ext. 225. The county's VITA page blocked automated access, so the 2027 schedule couldn't be checked. Call Aging Services.

name: Preserving Home (formerly Rebuilding Together of the Triangle) – Home Repairs
description: Nonprofit licensed contractor that does free critical repairs, accessibility changes and weatherization for low-income homeowners. It is also the front door for several city and county repair programs, matching each applicant to whatever funding fits.
access: Homeowners in Chatham, Durham, Orange or Wake counties who have owned and lived in the home at least 2 years, with property taxes paid. Income limits vary by program, up to 80% of area median income. Most programs require you to stay in the home 3 years after the work. Apply online, on a printable form (English or Spanish), or call for a paper application.
notes: Rebuilding Together of the Triangle is now called Preserving Home. It takes applications for City of Raleigh repair programs, Healthy Homes Cary, Habitat Greater Raleigh's Home Preservation program and Wake County's new Resilient Homes grants. Some programs have waitlists. Email: programs@preservehome.org.

name: Wake County Resilient Homes – Home Repair Grants
description: New Wake County grant program, launched in fall 2026 and run with Preserving Home. It pays for essential repairs such as weatherization, accessibility changes, radon and lead hazard fixes, wiring, plumbing, heating and cooling, unsafe stairs and roof damage, up to $35,000 per household.
access: Wake County homeowners outside Raleigh and Cary city limits. Household income below 50% of area median income ($52,950 for 2 people, $66,150 for 4), assets under $25,000 not counting the home, home on a permanent foundation, and property taxes current. Apply online through Preserving Home.
notes: Details come from CBS17 news coverage of the October 2026 launch. Wake County's own housing page still lists its older repair programs (Elderly & Disabled grants, Emergency Grant and Major Repair Loan, applied for through the Neighborly portal), which Resilient Homes is replacing. For county questions: housing.rehab@wake.gov or (919) 856-5906. Raleigh and Cary residents should use their city or town programs instead.

name: City of Raleigh – Limited Repair & Home Revitalization Programs
description: City-funded repairs for Raleigh homeowners, run by Preserving Home. Limited Repair fixes failing roofs, heating and cooling, electrical, plumbing or structure, typically up to $20,000. Home Revitalization covers broader repairs and accessibility in targeted neighborhoods, up to $30,000. Both are 0% deferred loans forgiven after 5 years.
access: Owner-occupied homes inside Raleigh city limits, valued at $389,500 or less ($450,000 or less for Revitalization). Limited Repair requires 5+ years of ownership and income up to $46,350 for 1 person ($87,350 for 8). Revitalization requires 10+ years of ownership, a home in a target area, and income up to $60,255 for 1 person.
notes: The larger Substantial Rehabilitation Program (for owners 62+ or disabled) is closed to new applications. Applications go to Preserving Home by mail (P.O. Box 4099, Cary, NC 27519), fax 919-651-0034 or email programs@preservehome.org. These are forgivable loans, not grants: the loan is repaid if you sell or move out within 5 years.

name: Healthy Homes Cary – Home Repair Program
description: Town of Cary program, run by Preserving Home, that pays for up to $12,500 in critical repairs for low- and moderate-income Cary homeowners: emergency roof or furnace replacement, energy-efficiency work, exterior repairs, accessibility and aging-in-place changes, and lead or asbestos hazards.
access: Cary homeowners with household income below 80% of area median income who have owned and lived in the home at least 2 years, with clear title and all property taxes and town fines paid. Apply through Preserving Home.
notes: Doesn't cover fire or smoke damage, new appliances, new construction or luxury upgrades.

name: Habitat for Humanity of Greater Raleigh – Home Preservation (repairs)
description: Habitat's repair program for existing homeowners in Wake County: leaking roofs, faulty wiring, weatherization, ramps and decks, HVAC, plumbing, flooring and siding, plus safety and accessibility changes.
access: Wake County homeowners who have lived in the home at least 2 years, are current on property taxes and agree to stay at least 3 years after the work. Apply through Preserving Home, which handles all intake. Habitat contacts the homeowners it selects.
notes: Formerly Habitat for Humanity of Wake County (habitatwake.org now redirects here). The page doesn't state income limits or cost to the homeowner, so check both when you apply. Email: homepres@habitatraleigh.org.

name: Habitat for Humanity of Orange County – Home Preservation Program (repairs)
description: Critical health and safety repairs at low or no cost: HVAC, roofs, sewer and septic, floors, water heaters, ramps, porch repairs and bathroom accessibility. Doesn't do cosmetic work.
address: 88 Vilcom Center Dr, Suite L110, Chapel Hill, NC 27514
access: Orange County homeowners living in the home, with household income below 80% of area median income (2026: $71,200 for 1 person, $101,700 for 4) and current on property taxes, insurance and mortgage. Email or mail the application (PDF on the site). Applying doesn't guarantee help.
notes: Email: repairs@orangehabitat.org. Orange Habitat is part of the Orange County Home Preservation Coalition, so the coalition's single screening form also reaches it.

name: Orange County Home Preservation Coalition (one form for home repair help)
description: One screening form that connects Orange County homeowners with a coalition of repair providers: the county Housing department and Department on Aging, Preserving Home, Orange Habitat, Hope Renovations, the Jackson Center, Central Pines, the towns of Chapel Hill, Carrboro and Hillsborough, and the UNC Community Practice Lab.
access: Orange County residents who need home repairs or modifications; many clients are older adults. Each partner program sets its own eligibility. Fill out the online screening form, or email ochpc@orangecountync.gov.
notes: If you meet the first criteria, a partner program calls to set up a home visit. Paper forms can also go to Preserving Home in Cary.

name: Orange County Housing – Urgent Repair & Single-Family Rehabilitation
description: County repair loans for low-income homeowners. Single-Family Rehabilitation makes larger repairs that extend a home's life (up to $70,000, a 0% deferred loan forgiven over 10–20 years). Urgent Repair fixes imminent safety threats and adds ramps (up to $10,000, forgiven over 5 years).
address: Whitted Building, 300 W Tryon St, 3rd floor, Hillsborough, NC 27278
access: Orange County homeowners living in the home, current on property taxes or on a payment plan. Rehab requires income at or below 80% of area median income, Urgent Repair at or below 50%. At least one must apply: owner 62+, a household member with a disability, an owner veteran, a child under 6 exposed to lead, or 5+ people in the household (Urgent Repair also counts single-parent households).
notes: Single-Family Rehabilitation is accepting applications for the 2026–2028 cycle. Urgent Repair is not taking applications right now. Also at the Southern Human Services Center, 2501 Homestead Rd, Chapel Hill. Email: housing_email@orangecountync.gov.

name: City of Durham Minor Repair Program (via Habitat for Humanity of Durham)
description: City-funded repairs for low-income Durham homeowners who are 62+ or disabled. Fixes conditions that threaten life, safety or accessibility: plumbing, roofs, ramps and railings, heating and air, electrical, floors, porches and gutters.
address: Habitat for Humanity of Durham, 1823 Chapel Hill Rd, Durham, NC 27707
access: Homeowners inside Durham city limits who are 62+ or disabled (with SSI or SSDI), have lived in the home at least 1 year, own no other residential property, and have income under 50% of area median income (FY2026: $44,500 for 1 person, $63,550 for 4). Manufactured homes aren't eligible.
notes: Download the application from Durham Habitat's website, then email it to repairs@durhamhabitat.org or mail or drop it off with your documents. The directory already lists Habitat for Humanity (Durham) in general; this entry is the city's repair program specifically.

name: Hope Renovations – Aging-in-Place Repairs & Construction Trades Training
description: Nonprofit that makes repairs and accessibility changes (grab bars, ramps, stair lifts, walk-in showers, wider doorways) priced on a sliding scale by household income. Market-rate clients help pay for subsidized work. It also runs a paid 13-week construction trades training for women and gender-expansive people.
address: 117 W Main St, Suite G, Carrboro, NC 27510 (workshop: 502A N Greensboro St)
access: Homeowners in Orange, Durham and Wake counties; the focus is older adults and people with disabilities. Request a project with the online form. Non-urgent requests in Durham and Wake are waitlisted; urgent requests are accepted on a rolling basis. Training is for women and gender-expansive people and pays a stipend.
notes: Email: info@hoperenovations.org. Hope Renovations is also a partner in the Orange County Home Preservation Coalition.

name: Durham County DSS – Energy Assistance (LIEAP & Crisis Intervention)
description: Help with heating and cooling bills. LIEAP is a once-a-year payment straight to your heating company. The Crisis Intervention Program (CIP) helps with past-due or cut-off accounts and new service when there's a heating or cooling emergency. Covers electric, natural gas, LP gas, kerosene and wood.
address: Durham County Human Services Building, 414 E Main St, 2nd floor, Lobby 27, Durham, NC 27701
access: Durham County households that meet income limits, with at least one U.S. citizen or eligible non-citizen. LIEAP opens in December for households with someone 60+ or someone disabled receiving adult services, then January–March for everyone, until funds run out. CIP requires a heating or cooling emergency. Apply online at epass.nc.gov, by mail or fax, or drop off a paper application.
notes: Mail to: Durham County DSS, AAS – Crisis Services-ENERGY Program, P.O. Box 810, Durham, NC 27701. Fax: 919-560-8120. The directory's existing Durham DSS Emergency Assistance listing covers rent and other crisis help.

name: Wake County Human Services – Energy & Utility Bill Assistance (LIEAP, CIP, Warmth for Wake)
description: One energy application covers LIEAP (a once-a-year heating payment, no past-due bill needed) and Crisis Intervention (CIP, for heating or cooling emergencies: past-due or disconnected service, or a deposit for new service). Warmth for Wake gives firewood or space heaters in winter, and Cool for Wake gives free fans in summer.
access: Wake County households that meet income guidelines. LIEAP runs December 2026–March 2027 (December for people 60+ or disabled receiving adult services, then January for everyone) until funds run out. CIP heating runs October–April and cooling May–September. Apply on ePASS (epass.nc.gov), by email to SS.Energy@wake.gov, by fax to 919-212-7085, or by mail. A case-manager interview is required.
notes: LIEAP payments take about 60 days to reach your utility. Families with children under 18 can get TANF-EA water help (applications opened November 2, 2026). For free weatherization, call Resources for Seniors at 919-713-1570. The directory already lists Wake County Human Services (Swinburne) in general.

name: Orange County DSS – Energy Assistance (LIEAP & Crisis Intervention)
description: LIEAP is a once-a-year heating-bill payment straight to your heating company. The Crisis Intervention Program helps with heating or cooling emergencies.
access: Orange County households responsible for their heating bill, with at least one U.S. citizen or eligible non-citizen, reserves at or below $2,250, and income under the limit. December 1–31 is for households with someone 60+ or disabled receiving adult services; January 1–March 31 is open to all until funds run out. Visit or call any Orange County DSS office, or apply at epass.nc.gov.
notes: The county page doesn't list income limits; NCDHHS uses 130% of the federal poverty level for LIEAP. Orange County DSS also has an office in Chapel Hill. The phone and address come from the NCDHHS county DSS directory.

name: Chatham County DSS – Energy Assistance (LIEAP & Crisis Intervention)
description: The county social services office that takes LIEAP (once-a-year heating help) and Crisis Intervention (heating or cooling emergency) applications for Chatham County residents.
access: Chatham County households under the income limit (LIEAP: 130% of the federal poverty level) who are responsible for heating costs. LIEAP opens in December for people 60+ or disabled receiving adult services, then January–March for all, until funds run out. Apply at epass.nc.gov or through DSS.
notes: Chatham County's own website blocked automated access, so the contact details come from the state DSS directory and the program rules from the NCDHHS LIEAP page (ncdhhs.gov/divisions/social-services/energy-assistance/low-income-energy-assistance-lieap). Fax: 919-542-6355. Call DSS to confirm dates.

name: Duke Energy Share the Light Fund
description: Duke Energy's donor-funded bill-assistance fund. Local partner agencies give eligible customers one-time help to avoid disconnection or keep service on. More than $1 million had gone out in North Carolina in 2026 as of April.
access: Duke Energy residential customers in financial hardship. You apply through a local partner agency, not through Duke. Eligibility is based on need.
notes: Duke's Share the Light page lists the partner agency for each county, but that list wouldn't load in our check (Nov 2026), so we couldn't confirm which agency takes applications in Durham, Wake, Orange or Chatham. Ask your county DSS energy office first. The source is Duke Energy's April 27, 2026 release.

name: Raleigh Water – Utility Customer Assistance Program (UCAP)
description: Up to $275 per fiscal year credited straight to a Raleigh Water account to help customers who are struggling with water and sewer bills. Wake County Human Services screens applicants.
address: Applications: Wake County Social Services, 220 Swinburne St, Raleigh, NC 27610 (drop box outside)
access: Raleigh Water customers (Raleigh, Garner, Knightdale, Wendell, Zebulon, Rolesville and Wake Forest) who qualify financially. Apply online in English or Spanish, mail the signed PDF form, or put it in the drop box. Help lasts until funds run out.
notes: UCAP helped 3,517 households in FY2026. Email: customercare@raleighnc.gov. The service-area towns come from Wake County's utility assistance page.

name: City of Durham Water Management – Water Hardship Assistance & Payment Plans
description: City-funded help with water bills. Situational hardship pays up to 75% of an eligible past-due balance (customer pays at least 25%) once per fiscal year. Monthly bill credits ($10 water + $10 sewer) go to qualifying elderly or disabled homeowners, disabled-veteran homeowners and Section 8 tenants. No-cost due-date extensions and installment plans are also available.
access: City of Durham residential water customers inside city limits. Apply online with proof of residency and eligibility documents. Monthly credits require a property-tax exemption (elderly/disabled or disabled veteran) or a Section 8 voucher, renewed each year.
notes: Hardship help doesn't cover deposits or penalties and is generally limited to two billing periods of average use, except for leaks that were promptly repaired. You can't get a payment plan and an installment arrangement at the same time.

name: OWASA Care to Share – Water Bill Assistance
description: Donor-funded program that helps Chapel Hill and Carrboro households facing hardship pay their OWASA water bills. OWASA also offers interest-free extended payment plans on past-due amounts, due-date changes and leak credits.
access: OWASA residential customers (Chapel Hill and Carrboro) having trouble paying. Call Customer Service to ask for Care to Share help. Every residential customer can get an extended payment plan.
notes: Email: customerinquiries@owasa.org. The payment-plan, due-date and leak-credit details come from owasa.org/save-water-save-money/.

name: NCWorks Career Center – Durham (Briggs Ave)
description: Free public job center with job search help, résumé help, career planning and work-readiness services. Also handles enrollment in WIOA-funded job training.
hours: Mon–Thu 8:30 am–5 pm; Fri 8:30 am–1 pm; 2nd & 3rd Wed open until 7 pm (pre-register for evening events)
access: Adults 18 and older
notes: Run by the City of Durham Office of Economic & Workforce Development. Self-service job-search and résumé satellite sites: CAARE (214 Broadway St.), Center for Employment Training (807 E. Main St.), Durham County Main Library (300 N. Roxboro St.), Durham Tech (1637 Lawson St.), NCCU Career Services (1801 Fayetteville St.), Oxford Manor (3633 Keystone Pl.) and W.D. Hill Recreation Center (1308 Fayetteville St.).

name: NCWorks Career Center – Raleigh (Tillery Place)
description: Free public job center with job search help, career services and access to training funds, run under the Capital Area Workforce Development Board.
access: Open to job seekers; call ahead
notes: Wake Local Reentry Council is based at this center. Capital Area NCWorks also runs a laid-off-worker Rapid Reskill grant and the yearly Triangle Career Expo (listed on capitalareancworks.com).

name: NCWorks Career Center – Raleigh Swinburne (Wake County Human Services)
description: Wake County's NCWorks center and Food & Nutrition Services Employment & Training (FNS E&T) office. Offers free computers, printing, faxing and phones, plus résumé review, practice interviews, career assessments, job fairs and help applying for WIOA training scholarships.
address: 220 Swinburne St., Room 3181 (3rd floor), Raleigh, NC 27610
hours: Mon–Thu 9 am–5 pm; Fri 9 am–2 pm
access: Wake County job seekers; walk in or call
notes: Email EmploymentFNS@wake.gov. Same building as Wake County Human Services (already listed separately).

name: NCWorks Career Center – Zebulon (Eastern Regional Center)
description: Free public job center in eastern Wake County: job search tools, résumé help, career assessments and training referrals.
access: Open to job seekers; call ahead
notes: Wake County's NCWorks page gives the address as 1001 Dogwood Drive (Eastern Regional Center) and the email dblevins@wake.gov.

name: NCWorks Career Center – Wake Forest (Northern Regional Center)
description: Free public job center in northern Wake County: job search tools, résumé help, career assessments and training referrals.
address: 350 E. Holding Ave., Wake Forest, NC 27587
access: Open to job seekers; call ahead
notes: Wake County's NCWorks page lists the phone as (919) 562-6379 and the email ryeager@wake.gov.

name: NCWorks Career Center – Fuquay-Varina (Southern Regional Center)
description: Free public job center in southern Wake County: job search tools, résumé help, career assessments and training referrals.
address: 130 N. Judd Parkway NE, Fuquay-Varina, NC 27526
access: Open to job seekers; call ahead
notes: Wake County's NCWorks page lists the phone as (919) 557-1002 and the email richard.hayner@wake.gov.

name: Orange County Skills Development Center / NCWorks Career Center
description: Free one-stop career center with career assessment and counseling, workshops, training and education information, hiring events, unemployment claim filing, employment help for people with disabilities and a career resource library.
address: 203 S. Greensboro St., 3rd floor (Drakeford Library Complex), Carrboro, NC 27510
access: Open to the public
notes: Email sdcjoblink@orangecountync.gov. Free parking. Durham Tech also runs free P.I.V.O.T. job-skills classes at its Orange County campus (see Durham Tech workforce listing).

name: Durham Tech – Free Workforce (HRD) Job Skills Courses
description: Short job-readiness classes: Career Readiness Certificate prep, P.I.V.O.T. employability training, Resumes That Work!, Technology Awareness and Workforce Ready Reentry (HRD-3003F), which serves people who are justice-involved.
hours: Varies by class; fall 2026 P.I.V.O.T. sections meet Wednesdays
access: Fees are waived if you are unemployed, have a layoff notice, or are working and either EITC-eligible or earning at or below 200% of the federal poverty level. Register with the HRD Fee Waiver Verification Form.
notes: Contact: Candace Rashada, Director, rashadac@durhamtech.edu, Wynn Building 10, Room 109B. Some sections meet at the Orange County campus. Spring 2027 registration is open. Workforce Ready Reentry: https://www.durhamtech.edu/courses/workforce-ready-reentry ($70 fee, waived for eligible students). Durham Tech's ESL classes are listed separately.

name: Wake Tech – Free Career Workshops & Propel Workforce Training
description: Wake Tech Career Services runs short courses and workshops on résumés, cover letters, interviews, LinkedIn and job search. The Propel scholarship pays for short (3–6 month) credential courses in high-demand fields.
hours: Career coaches hold drop-in hours at campuses, no reservation needed
access: Fees waived for NC residents 18+ who are unemployed, underemployed, facing a layoff, EITC-eligible, or earning at or below 200% of the federal poverty level. Propel is for students with financial need. Register with NCWorks first.
notes: Propel details: https://waketech.edu/freetraining. Awards cover registration and fees up to $750 per course, for up to 3 courses on one pathway. Main college line: (919) 866-5000.

name: StepUp Ministry – Employment & Life Skills Academies
description: Free Employment Academy (weekly ENER-G sessions, boot camps, case management, employer placements) and Life Skills Academy (budgeting, credit restoration, goal setting). Also runs youth programs and GG's Closet interview clothing. Many participants are seeking a second chance after incarceration.
hours: Cohorts start on set dates (2026 Employment Academy starts were June 23, July 28, Sept. 15 and Oct. 2); prospective-participant tour Nov. 10, 2026
access: Employment Academy requires a valid ID and Social Security card, no pending charges, 30 days clean and sober, 45 days removed from domestic violence, and not being on the sex offender registry. Boot camps are free for ages 18–60. Enroll online.
notes: Started by White Memorial Presbyterian Church. Its values say lives are transformed 'through God's love and grace', but the site lists no required religious activity. Email info@stepupministry.org. Campbell Law's clinic has held free expunction clinics with StepUp.

name: StepUp Durham – Job Readiness & Coaching
description: Free Job Readiness Week workshop, one-on-one job coaching, employer referrals and supportive services, followed by weekly ENER-G meetings with employers and financial coaching. Step2 helps working graduates build savings and careers.
address: 112 Broadway St., Suite B (ReCity Network), Durham, NC 27701
access: Durham job seekers facing barriers to work, including a criminal background or gaps in work history. Starts with a one-hour intake conversation. Register online or by phone.
notes: Separate affiliate of StepUp Ministry. Its values say lives are transformed 'through God's love and grace', but the site lists no required religious activity. Email info@stepupdurham.org.

name: Dress for Success Triangle – Raleigh
description: Free career coaching, workplace clothing and styling, training and certificate programs (including the 5-week virtual Going Places Network), and career webinars for women.
hours: Wed & Thu 10 am–4 pm; 2nd Saturdays 10 am–4 pm
access: Women seeking work or career growth. Start career coaching with an online assessment.
notes: The Durham location (701 William Vickers Ave.) is already in the directory. A mobile boutique also visits sites in Eastern NC.

name: Durham Local Reentry Council (Durham County Justice Services)
description: Reentry case management for people coming home from prison or jail: job readiness and placement help, short-term or transitional housing help, transportation, substance use and mental health referrals, child-care help and other basic needs.
address: Justice Services Department, 326 E. Main St., Durham, NC 27701
access: Justice-involved Durham residents who need reentry services, and people within 6 months of release with a Durham home plan. Walk in and ask for the LRC Coordinator or Case Manager, or call for an appointment. Self-referrals accepted.
notes: Email durhamlrc@dconc.gov. The state Division of Adult Correction's council list also gives (919) 560-7589.

name: City of Durham Welcome Home Program (reentry peer support)
description: Peer support for people returning to Durham after incarceration. Helps with IDs, birth certificates, Social Security cards, Medicaid and food benefits, job readiness and placement, and housing. Some participants receive a Welcome Home box of essentials.
access: Adults 18+ returning to Durham from state or federal prison, or from 9+ consecutive months in Durham County jail, who were released within the last 90 days. Referral form online, or contact staff.
notes: Part of the City of Durham Community Safety Department. Program manager: Kristi Riley (kristi.riley@durhamnc.gov). Peer specialists: (919) 698-8454, (919) 698-8260, (984) 383-2316.

name: Wake Local Reentry Council
description: Reentry help with basic needs, driver's license restoration, behavioral health navigation, vocational training, peer support, transportation, housing assistance and life skills workshops.
address: 1830-B Tillery Place, Raleigh, NC 27604 (NCWorks Career Center)
access: Wake County residents 18+ who were justice-involved within the last 5 years. Self-referrals and agency referrals by online form.
notes: Email WakeLRC@wake.gov. Run through the Capital Area Workforce Development Board, per the NC Division of Adult Correction's council list.

name: Orange County Local Reentry Council
description: Reentry case management, help with immediate needs, goal-setting action plans, and housing, employment and transportation support. Also connects people to community resources and substance use treatment.
address: Whitted Human Services Building, Office B242, 300 N. Tryon St., Hillsborough, NC 27278
access: Anyone returning to Orange County from state or federal prison or local jail, before or after release. Also Orange County residents facing barriers from past justice involvement. Online referral form.
notes: Run by the Orange County Criminal Justice Resource Department. Coordinator Tiffany Bullard (tbullard@orangecountync.gov). Case manager Trina Ford-Raynor, (919) 717-1198. Recidivism Reduction Call Center: 1-888-852-0004.

name: Chatham/Lee Local Reentry Council
description: State-funded local reentry council that connects people to resources during and after release from prison.
access: People returning to Chatham County from incarceration. Call the reentry coordinator.
notes: The state list names Lee County Community Support Services as the intermediary agency. Contacts: Kimberly.jones@chathamcountync.gov, (984) 351-0675 / (919) 545-1990, and james.martin@chathamcountync.gov. Chatham County's own reentry page blocked automated access, so services and office location could not be confirmed there.

name: Orange County Restoration Legal Counsel (expunctions & license restoration)
description: Free county attorney who handles expunctions, certificates of relief, court debt relief, driver's license restoration, and probation and court fee relief.
address: Criminal Justice Resource Department, 106 E. Margaret Lane, Courthouse basement, Hillsborough, NC 27278
access: Orange County residents. Contact the attorney directly or submit the referral form.
notes: Attorney Mitchell Lucas, mlucas@orangecountync.gov, alternate (919) 451-0281. CJRD main line: (919) 245-2310.

name: Criminal Justice Debt Program (Carrboro / Chapel Hill / Orange County)
description: Pays court fees and costs (in NC or other states) and NC DMV hearing and license reinstatement fees for low-income Orange County residents, so they can get their license back and stabilize after justice involvement.
access: Orange County residents who meet court indigency standards, are not incarcerated, have already tried other relief (such as license restoration), can show the help will make an immediate difference, and have not received CJDP funds in the last 3 years. Apply online.
notes: Carrboro residents call the Carrboro Program Administrator at (919) 918-7397. Other Orange County residents call the Chapel Hill Police Crisis Unit at (919) 968-2806. Fines, restitution and vehicle registration costs are not covered. Funded by Chapel Hill, Carrboro and the Orange County Bail Bond Justice Project.

name: Durham County Veteran Services
description: County veterans service officers explain federal, state and local veterans benefits to veterans and their families. They help fill out VA claim forms and gather supporting documents for disability, health care, education, dependent and survivor benefits and property-tax relief.
access: Veterans and their family members. Call, email veteranservices@dconc.gov or use the online request form.
notes: Hours aren't posted, so call first. The office sometimes runs with limited services during staff accreditation training, as it did in April 2026. The page doesn't mention fees. County service officers are VA-accredited and don't charge for claims help.

name: Wake County Veterans Services
description: County veterans service officers help with VA disability claims and benefits, VA health care enrollment, state benefits, and veterans' employment and housing resources. Virtual and phone appointments are available on request.
hours: Mon–Fri 8:30 am–5:15 pm; walk-ins 9 am–4 pm
access: Wake County veterans and their families only. All claims help needs an appointment (book online or call). Walk-ins are limited to DMV tags, hunting and fishing licenses, and property-tax exemption forms. For claims, bring your DD-214, a voided check, your marriage license, dependents' birth certificates and your medical records.
notes: Satellite offices: Northern Regional Center, Wake Forest (Tue/Wed/Thu 9 am–4 pm) and Eastern Regional Center, Zebulon (Mon/Tue/Thu 9 am–4 pm). Email veterans@wake.gov. The page doesn't mention fees. County service officers are VA-accredited and don't charge for claims help. The page also lists 9 am–4 pm operating hours, so call ahead to confirm.

name: Orange County Veteran Services
description: The county Veteran Services Officer helps with VA disability compensation, dependent and survivor benefits, burial, education and housing benefits, VA health care enrollment, and preparing claims paperwork.
access: Veterans, their dependents and family members, surviving spouses and children, Guard and Reserve members, and active-duty service members. Eligibility depends on service history, discharge status and the benefit. Call or email vso@orangecountync.gov for an appointment, in person or remote.
notes: The county page says "Services are provided at no cost." The in-person address comes from the county's Applying for Services page (https://orangecountync.gov/1830/Applying-for-Services). Hours aren't posted.

name: Chatham County Veteran Services
description: The county Veteran Services Officer, Stephanie Briggs, advocates for veterans and their families and helps them apply for VA and state benefits.
access: Chatham County veterans and their families. Call for an appointment.
notes: The county website blocks automated access, so the address and phone come from the search-index text of the county page. Briggs is confirmed as VSO by a WPTF interview from Nov. 11, 2025 (https://rss.com/podcasts/wptf-morning-show/2321887). There is also a satellite at the Siler City Center for Active Living, 112 Village Lake Rd., Siler City, on Wednesdays. Posted hours disagree between sources, so call first. Email: stephanie.briggs@chathamcountync.gov.

name: Veterans Bridge Home – Triangle
description: Nonprofit navigators for service members, veterans and military families. They build a plan with you and connect you to help with housing, employment, VA benefits, health care, financial stability and other community resources.
access: Service members, veterans, spouses, caregivers and families of any service era, discharge status or disability level. There are no income requirements. Submit a Request for Assistance online or call. This is not an emergency service: for a crisis, dial 988 and press 1.
notes: The Triangle team covers Chatham, Durham, Orange, Wake and six other counties. The FAQ says there are no income restrictions and that the group supports veterans "without imposing financial barriers." Some housing resources it refers people to have their own income limits. Email: info@veteransbridgehome.org.

name: Campbell Law Veterans Legal Clinic
description: Free legal representation from supervised Campbell Law students, launched in August 2025. It helps low-income former service members correct injustices in their military records, such as discharge upgrades.
access: Low-income former service members. Apply through the online intake form linked from the clinic page, or email vlc@campbell.edu.
notes: Upper-level law students do the work under a licensed attorney's supervision. Capacity is limited.

name: NCCU School of Law – Veterans Law Clinic
description: Supervised law students represent low-income veterans in VA disability compensation claims and appeals (including to the Board of Veterans' Appeals), discharge upgrades and character-of-discharge decisions. It is run with UNC School of Law.
access: Low-income veterans, and in some matters their family members. Representation isn't guaranteed and depends on clinic capacity and case type. Call to ask about eligibility or an appointment.
notes: The clinic page doesn't state fees. NCCU and UNC describe it as a grant-funded clinic providing free legal services to veterans. It is at NCCU's law school in Durham.

name: UNC School of Law – Military and Veterans Law Clinic
description: Supervised law students help former service members upgrade Other Than Honorable and Bad Conduct discharges that block VA health care and disability benefits.
access: Only low-income former service members with discharge-type or characterization problems. Capacity is limited and help isn't guaranteed. Call to start.
notes: The page doesn't mention fees. UNC law clinics serve low-income clients, and UNC described the clinic as offering free representation. A Nov. 2025 UNC Research story confirms it is active. Current UNC students should call Carolina Student Legal Services instead.

name: Triangle Family Services – Financial Counseling
description: Free one-on-one financial counseling from certified counselors: budgeting, emergency savings, fixed-income budgeting, credit report review, debt payoff and credit rebuilding. Also offers workshops. TFS is a HUD-approved housing counseling agency and an NFCC member.
access: Individuals and families across the greater Triangle. You don't need to be in another TFS program. Meet in person, by phone or virtually. Call or email kentonjones@tfsnc.org for an appointment.
notes: TFS also runs housing-security case management and street outreach for people experiencing homelessness, and outpatient therapy.

name: EMPOWERment, Inc. – Housing Counseling
description: HUD-certified housing counseling at no cost: homebuyer education classes, help with buying a first home, refinancing and avoiding foreclosure, and budgeting counseling. The group also owns affordable rentals in Orange County that accept Housing Choice Vouchers.
address: 109 N. Graham St., Suite 200, Chapel Hill, NC 27516
access: Call or use the contact form for an appointment.
notes: The group's M.O.M. Emergency Utility Fund (Orange County residents, bills up to $500, once every 12 months) had no funds available when checked. Hours are from https://www.empowermentinc.org/contact.
